title: Apache Airflow DAGs
description: For Apache Airflow DAGs: idempotent tasks, light top-level code, credentials in connections or a secrets backend, a DAG loader test, installs with the constraints file and care when removing a task.

sources.title: Apache Airflow documentation, installation from PyPI

rules.instruction: Write each task like a database transaction: Airflow can retry a failed task, so a re-run must produce the same outcome and a failure must leave no partial result, for example by replacing a partition instead of appending to it.
rules.verification: Run the changed task twice for the same logical date in a test environment and check that the second run leaves the same data as the first.

rules.instruction: Keep the top level of a DAG file to what creates operators and their dependencies: no database access, network call or heavy computation, no `Variable.get()` (read a variable with a template such as `{{ var.value.name }}` in the task), and move expensive imports into the task callables.
rules.verification: Review the top level of each DAG file the change edits for database, network or `Variable.get()` calls and heavy imports, and check its parse time in the DAG processor.

rules.instruction: Store no password or token in a task or a DAG file: reach systems through Airflow connections by their connection id, and keep sensitive variables in a secrets backend.
rules.verification: Search the change for passwords, tokens and keys written in DAG files and check that each system is reached through a connection id.

rules.instruction: Keep a test that loads the project's DAGs with `DagBag` and fails on any import error, and run it in CI, so that a missing dependency or a syntax error never reaches the scheduler.
rules.verification: task verify checks that a test under `tests/` uses `DagBag`; also check that CI runs it and that it reports no import error for the change.

rules.instruction: When the project installs Airflow with pip, pin `apache-airflow` and install it with `--constraint` pointing at the constraints file of that Airflow and Python version; install the providers afterwards, still pinning Airflow.
rules.verification: Check that the install command or requirements pin `apache-airflow` and use the constraints file of the same Airflow and Python versions.

rules.instruction: Before removing a task from a DAG, decide whether its past logs must stay reachable: a removed task no longer shows in the Graph and Grid views, so its logs are hard to reach from the web server. To keep them, create a new DAG instead.
rules.verification: For a change that removes a task, check that the change says whether its past logs must stay reachable and, if so, that a new DAG replaces the old one.
